parts.text: Which claim correctly classifies the changes?

options.text: Melting the ice is reversible because the ice can be brought back; chopping the carrot is not reversible because the whole carrot cannot be brought back.
Chopping the carrot is reversible because the carrot material is still there.
Melting the ice is not reversible.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Bharti melts some ice to water and later freezes the water back to ice. She also chops a carrot into small pieces.

part_answers.answer: A change is reversible only if the original object or substance can be brought back. Ice can be recovered by freezing; the whole chopped carrot cannot.

teacher.key_rationale: Reversibility asks whether the original object or substance can be brought back. Melting ice can be reversed by freezing; chopping cannot restore the whole carrot. Keeping the material alone does not make chopping reversible, and melting is reversible.
